raw_case_text:
A 62 year-old man with a 16 year history of well-controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus, a 10 year history of hypertension, and a 13 year history of chronic kidney disease (on thrice-weekly hemodialysis for the past 4 years) was admitted on 20 October 2023 with a 4 day history of altered consciousness and an 11 day history of intermittent fever that had initially been overlooked until neurological deterioration prompted prior hospitalization, where empirical antimicrobial therapy proved ineffective. Three years after total gastrectomy for gastric cancer, he was transferred to our intensive care unit (ICU) with pancytopenia (white blood cells [WBCs]: 1.90 x 109/L, red blood cells [RBCs]: 4.11 x 1012/L, and platelets [PLTs]): 9 x 109/L), hypoalbuminemia (31.7 g/L), and acute-on-chronic renal failure (creatinine: 445.9 mumol/L). Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed multifocal abnormal signals in the bilateral frontoparietal cortices and semioval centers (Figure 1), while chest computed tomography (CT) showed miliary nodules, left upper-lobe consolidation, and right lower-lobe bronchiectasis. CSF analyzed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) yielded MTB DNA, confirming tuberculous meningitis. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) obtained via bedside bronchoscopy was positive on GeneXpert MTB/RIF (rifampicin-susceptible, "low" detection level); mNGS additionally identified Streptococcus pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Aspergillus, Pneumocystis jirovecii, and MTB DNA sequences, supporting miliary TB. Subsequent cultures of both BALF and CSF confirmed growth of MTB, while BALF also yielded Aspergillus fumigatus with a positive galactomannan (GM) antigen test, indicating concomitant invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. Final diagnoses were CNS TB, miliary pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, and polymicrobial pulmonary coinfection.
Owing to preexisting bone-marrow suppression, linezolid, known to worsen cytopenias, was avoided in favor of contezolid. Because voriconazole was required for concurrent fungal infections and rifampicin markedly reduces voriconazole plasma concentrations, rifampicin was excluded from the initial regimen. The anti-TB regimen comprised isoniazid 300 mg once daily, pyrazinamide 1500 mg once daily, contezolid 400 mg twice daily, and cycloserine 250 mg twice daily, supplemented with voriconazole 200 mg twice daily for antifungal therapy. All medications were administered after hemodialysis sessions. PLT transfusions and other hematopoietic supportive measures were provided. The patient improved clinically within 6 days, with resolution of fever and restoration of consciousness. Follow-up laboratory tests showed hematological recovery: WBCs: 5.09 x 109/L, RBCs: 4.13 x 1012/L, and PLTs: 54 x 109/L. After stabilization, he was discharged to continue thrice-weekly hemodialysis.
At the 2-month follow-up, the patient reported fatigue and a new-onset cough of 1-week duration, without fever or neurological symptoms. Examination revealed no recurrence of CNS infection. CSF parameters remained stable compared to previous results (Figure 2), and cultures were negative, confirming controlled tuberculous meningitis. Chest CT showed progressive bilateral pulmonary infiltrates (Figure 3(b)). BALF mNGS detected spore-forming bacteria, prompting initiation of cotrimoxazole 960 mg three times daily after respiratory consultation. Drawing on the experience of linezolid dose adjustment in TB treatment in the literature and considering the patient's limited financial resources, we reduced contezolid to 400 mg once daily. After 3 weeks of therapy and clinical improvement, cotrimoxazole was discontinued. Subsequent chest CT on 22 February 2024 demonstrated marked lesion resolution (Figure 3(c)). At the March review, he remained asymptomatic with normal findings. CSF profiles were stable from baseline (Figure 2), with negative MTB cultures from CSF and BALF, and no pathogens detected by mNGS. After clinical assessment confirmed cure of pulmonary aspergillosis, voriconazole was stopped, and anti-TB therapy was adjusted to rifampicin 600 mg once daily, isoniazid 300 mg once daily, pyrazinamide 1500 mg once daily, and cycloserine 250 mg twice daily. Follow-up has shown continued clinical stability, with chest CT on 17 January 2025 revealing unchanged pulmonary findings (Figure 3(d)). Throughout treatment, WBC and PLT counts fluctuated within safe ranges, while CSF cellularity and protein normalized (Figure 2). All microbiological results are summarized in Table 1. Key clinical events, examination findings, and treatment regimens are depicted in Figure 2. Anti-TB therapy was completed on 2 March 2025, with ongoing surveillance planned.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 62-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis presented on October 20, 2023, with an 11-day history of intermittent fever and a 4-day history of altered consciousness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed intermittent fever 11 days prior to ICU admission, which was initially overlooked until he developed altered mental status 4 days prior to presentation. He was briefly hospitalized at a local facility where empirical antibiotics proved ineffective, prompting transfer to our ICU on October 20, 2023.
subjective.past_medical_history: Well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (16 years); hypertension (10 years); end-stage chronic kidney disease (13 years, on thrice-weekly maintenance hemodialysis for 4 years); gastric cancer status post total gastrectomy 3 years prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for intermittent fever and altered consciousness on initial admission; at 2-month follow-up, positive for fatigue and a 1-week new-onset cough without fever or neurological symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Impaired consciousness on initial ICU admission (restored within 6 days of targeted therapy).
objective.routine_investigations: ICU admission laboratory tests: Severe pancytopenia with WBC 1.90 x 10^9/L, RBC 4.11 x 10^12/L, and platelets 9 x 10^9/L (recovering by day 6 to WBC 5.09 x 10^9/L, RBC 4.13 x 10^12/L, PLT 54 x 10^9/L); hypoalbuminemia (31.7 g/L); and elevated serum creatinine (445.9 μmol/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI: Multifocal abnormal signals in the bilateral frontoparietal cortices and centrum semiovale. Admission chest CT: Bilateral miliary nodules, left upper lobe consolidation, and right lower lobe bronchiectasis. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) mNGS and culture: Positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) DNA and subsequent MTB culture growth. Bedside bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) analysis: Positive GeneXpert MTB/RIF (rifampicin-susceptible, low level); BALF mNGS identified DNA sequences of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Aspergillus, Pneumocystis jirovecii, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa; BALF cultures grew MTB and Aspergillus fumigatus with a positive BALF galactomannan (GM) antigen test. Two-month follow-up chest CT and repeat BALF mNGS: Progressive bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with spore-forming bacteria detected on BALF mNGS.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated miliary pulmonary tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis (confirmed by CSF and BALF mNGS, GeneXpert MTB/RIF, and MTB cultures) with concomitant invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (confirmed by BALF Aspergillus fumigatus culture and galactomannan) and polymicrobial pulmonary co-infection including Pneumocystis jirovecii, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (detected on BALF mNGS) in a hemodialysis patient with baseline pancytopenia. Plan and clinical course: To avoid linezolid-induced myelosuppression and rifampicin-voriconazole CYP450 drug interactions, initial post-dialysis therapy was tailored to isoniazid (300 mg qd), pyrazinamide (1,500 mg qd), contezolid (400 mg bid), cycloserine (250 mg bid), and voriconazole (200 mg bid), supported by platelet transfusions. Consciousness and fever resolved within 6 days with hematologic recovery, and he was discharged on maintenance hemodialysis. At 2-month follow-up, new-onset cough and progressive bilateral infiltrates responded to a 3-week course of oral co-trimoxazole (TMP-SMX 960 mg tid) and dose-reduced contezolid (400 mg qd), achieving marked CT resolution by February 22, 2024. In March 2024, after confirming cure of aspergillosis and negative CSF/BALF MTB cultures and mNGS, voriconazole and contezolid were stopped and he completed a standard rifampicin (600 mg qd), isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and cycloserine regimen on March 2, 2025.
